texts.error.bitmap: A picture in AppleWin's resources is damaged.
texts.error.bitmap_layout: A picture in AppleWin's resources is laid out in a way this core does not read.
texts.error.card_key: The Super Serial Card's saved state lacks '%1'.
texts.error.not_built: AppleWin could not build the machine: %1
texts.firmware.apple2_jplus_rom.about: The ROM of the Japanese Apple II j-plus, with its katakana monitor (12 KB). It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2_JPlus.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2_jplus_video_rom.about: The character ROM of the Apple II j-plus, with its katakana (2 KB). It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2_JPlus_Video.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2_plus_rom.about: The ROM of the Apple II Plus (12 KB). It holds the autostart monitor and Applesoft BASIC. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2_Plus.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2_rom.about: The ROM of the original Apple II (12 KB). It holds the old monitor and Integer BASIC. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2_video_rom.about: The character ROM of the Apple II and II Plus (2 KB). It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2_Video.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2e_enhanced_rom.about: The system ROM of the enhanced Apple IIe, the 65C02 machine of 1985 (16 KB). It holds the monitor program, Applesoft BASIC and the 80-column firmware. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2e_Enhanced.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2e_enhanced_video_rom.abou: The character ROM of the (enhanced) Apple IIe (4 KB). It holds the shapes of the text and MouseText characters. Both IIe models and the TK3000 //e use it. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2e_Enhanced_Video.rom.
texts.firmware.apple2e_rom.about: The system ROM of the original (unenhanced) Apple IIe (16 KB). It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Apple2e.rom.
texts.firmware.base64a_german_video_rom.about: The character ROM of the Base 64A, with the German character set (4 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Base64A_German_Video.rom.
texts.firmware.base64a_rom.about: The ROM of the Copam Base 64A, the Taiwanese Apple II Plus clone, which has its own monitor (48 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Base64A.rom.
texts.firmware.charset82_bmp.about: The character set of the Pravets 82, as the 1-bit bitmap AppleWin stores it in (8254 bytes). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/CHARSET82.bmp.
texts.firmware.charset8c_bmp.about: The two character sets of the Pravets 8A/8C, as the 1-bit bitmap AppleWin stores them in (16446 bytes). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/CHARSET8C.bmp.
texts.firmware.charset8m_bmp.about: The character set of the Pravets 8M, as the 1-bit bitmap AppleWin stores it in (8254 bytes). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/CHARSET8M.bmp.
texts.firmware.disk2_rom.about: The boot ROM of the Disk II controller card in slot 6 (256 bytes, the chip called P5). It reads the first track and starts a disk. Every machine here has the card, so the file is always needed. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/DISK2.rom.
texts.firmware.parallel_rom.about: The firmware of the parallel printer card (256 bytes), which AppleWin puts in slot 1 by default. It is needed as long as the Printer card setting keeps the card. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/Parallel.rom.
texts.firmware.pravets82_rom.about: The ROM of the Pravets 82, the Bulgarian Apple II Plus (12 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/PRAVETS82.ROM.
texts.firmware.pravets8c_rom.about: The ROM of the Pravets 8A/8C, the Bulgarian Apple IIe (16 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/PRAVETS8C.ROM.
texts.firmware.pravets8m_rom.about: The ROM of the Pravets 8M (12 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/PRAVETS8M.ROM.
texts.firmware.ssc_rom.about: The firmware of Apple's Super Serial Card (2 KB), which AppleWin puts in slot 2 by default. It is needed as long as the Serial card setting keeps the card. It is Apple's and you have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/SSC.rom.
texts.firmware.tk3000e_rom.about: The ROM of the Microdigital TK3000 //e, the Brazilian Apple IIe (16 KB). You have to supply it. AppleWin's source has it as resource/TK3000e.rom.
texts.setting.enhancediskspeed.about: On (AppleWin's default), the Disk II drive reads at full speed and not at the speed of a real drive. Off gives the real drive's timing. Either way the timing is the same on every computer.
texts.setting.halfscanlines.about: Draws every second line dark, to look like a picture tube. AppleWin has this on by default. It is off here, because Chimera scales a full picture better.
texts.setting.joystick1.about: A joystick in the game port (the P1 axes and buttons). With none plugged in, the paddle inputs read as not connected, which some programs need.
texts.setting.joystick2.about: A second joystick (the P2 axes and button). Plugging it in changes how the buttons are shared between the joysticks, as on the real machine.
texts.setting.memorypattern.about: What the memory holds when the machine is switched on. A real Apple's memory holds a pattern that depends on its memory chips. AppleWin's default alternates FF FF 00 00. 'random' takes its values from the Random Seed, so they are the same every time.
texts.setting.mockingboard.about: A Mockingboard sound card in slot 4 (AppleWin's default), in slots 4 and 5, in slot 5 only, or none.
texts.setting.mockingboardvolume.about: The volume of the Mockingboard, in percent. It changes the sound output only.
texts.setting.model.about: Which Apple II this is. The choices are the enhanced //e (with a 65C02 processor, the machine most software expects), the original //e, the ][+ and the ][ (6502 processor, no lowercase letters, no 80 columns), the Japanese ][ J-Plus, and the clones AppleWin knows. The model decides the ROM, the processor and the keyboard.
texts.setting.printer.about: A parallel printer card in slot 1, as AppleWin has by default, or an empty slot. The card's firmware is the Parallel.rom file the core asks for. It is part of the machine, because a program that checks the slot sees the difference.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The starting number of the random generator that AppleWin's disk emulation uses for the noise a Disk II drive reads between valid data. A movie records the number it ran with.
texts.setting.refreshrate.about: 60 Hz is an NTSC Apple (17030 processor cycles per frame, 1.0205 MHz). 50 Hz is a PAL Apple (20280 cycles, 1.0156 MHz). It changes the frame rate and the machine's timing.
texts.setting.serial.about: A Super Serial Card in slot 2, as AppleWin has by default, or an empty slot. The card's firmware is the SSC.rom file the core asks for. It is part of the machine, because a program that checks the slot sees the difference.
texts.setting.speakervolume.about: The volume of the Apple's speaker, in percent. It changes the sound output only.
texts.setting.video.about: How the picture is drawn: as on a colour television (with NTSC colour effects, AppleWin's default), a colour monitor, idealised colour, an RGB card or a monochrome monitor. A program runs the same with any of them. The picture a movie shows is different, so the setting is recorded with the machine.
texts.slot.floppy1.help: Disk images for drive 1 (slot 6). Accepted are DOS-order images (.dsk, .do), ProDOS-order images (.po), nibble images (.nib), .woz images and 140K .2mg images. The machine starts from the first one. The order here is the order the Next Disk 1 input goes through.
texts.slot.floppy2.help: Disk images for drive 2. The first one is in the drive when the machine starts, and the Next Disk 2 input goes through the rest.
texts.slot.harddisk.help: Up to two ProDOS hard disk images, on a controller card in slot 7. What the machine writes is kept in memory and saved in savestates. The file itself is never changed.
